Χριστός.sd: anointed, i.e. the Messiah, an epithet of Jesus
Χριστός.as:
χριστός (Χρ-), -ή, -όν
(< χρίω), [in LXX for מָשִׁיחַ and cogn. forms ;]
1. as adj.,
(a) of things, anointing, to be used as ointment (Æsch., Eur., al.; τ. ἔλαιον τὸ χ., Le 21:10);
(b) of persons, anointed (ὁ ἰερεὺς ὁ χ., Le 4:5; οἱ χ. ἰευρεῖς, II Mac 1:10): ὁ χ. τοῦ κυρίου or Θεοῦ (I Ki 2:10, Ps 2:2, al.), of the Messiah (Aram., מְשִׁיחָא; cf. Dalman, Words, 289 ff.), Lk 2:11, 26Jo 1:41, Ac 2:364:26, al.
2. As subst., ὁ Χριστός, the Messiah, the Christ: Mt 2:4, Mk 8:29, Lk 2:11, Jo 1:20, Ac 2:31, Ro 7:4, al.; Ἰησοῦς Χ., Mk 1:1, Jo 1:17, Ac 2:38, al.; Χ. Ἰησοῦς, Mt 1:18, WH, mg. Ac 5:42, Ro 6:3, al.; Χ. κύριος, Lk 2:11; Ἰησοῦς Χ. ὁ κύριος, Ac 15:26, Ro 1:7, al.

χρόνος.sd: a space of time (in general, and thus properly distinguished from G2540 (καιρός), which designates a fixed or special occasion; and from G165 (αἰών), which denotes a particular period) or interval; by extension, an individual opportunity; by implication, delay
χρόνος.kj: + years old, season, space, (X often-)time(-s), (a) while
χρόνος.as:
χρόνος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for יוֹם, also for עֵת, etc. ;]
time (a space of time, whether long or short; cf. Lft., Notes, 70): Mt 2:7, Mk 9:21, Lk 1:57, Ac 3:217:17, 2313:1817:3027:9, He 11:32, I Pe 1:174:3, Re 10:6; στιγμὴ χρόνου, Lk 4:5; πλήρωμα τοῦ χ., Ga 4:4; ποιεῖν χ., Ac 15:3318:23; βιῶσαι, I Pe 4:2; διδόναι, Re 2:21; pl., χ. καὶ (ἢ) καιροί (Lft., l.c.), Ac 1:7, I Th 5:1; ἐπ’ ἐσχάτου τῶν χ. (χρόνου), I Pe 1:20, Ju 18; c. prep., ἄχρι, Ac 3:21; διὰ τὸν χ., He 5:12; ἐν χ., Ac 1:6, 21; ἐπὶ (πλείονα) χ., Lk 18:4, Ac 18:20; ἐφ’ ὅσον χ., Ro 7:1, I Co 7:39, Ga 4:1; κατὰ τὸν χ., Mt 2:16; μετὰ τολὺν (τοσοῦτον) χ., Mt 25:19, He 4:7; πρὸ χ. αἰωςίων, II Ti 1:9, Tit 1:2, instr. dat. of extension of time (v. M, Pr., 75, 148; Deiss., LAE, 206), Lk 8:27, 29Jo 14:9, Ac 8:11, Ro 16:25; acc, of duration of time, Mk 2:19, Lk 20:9, Jo 5:67:3312:3514:9, Ac 14:3, 2819:2220:18, I Co 16:7, Re 6:11.†
SYN.: v.s. καιρός

χαίρω.long: I rejoice, am glad; also a salutation: Hail.
χαίρω.sd: to be "cheer"ful, i.e. calmly happy or well-off; impersonally, especially as salutation (on meeting or parting), be well
χαίρω.kj: farewell, be glad, God speed, greeting, hall, joy(- fully), rejoice
χαίρω.as:
χαίρω
[in LXX for שָׂמַח (Ge 45:16, al.), גִּיל (Pr 2:14, al.), etc.; inf., as greeting (v. infr.), Is 48:2257:21שָׁלוֹם), I Mac 10:18, II Mac 1:1 and freq. in these books ;]
1.to rejoice, be glad: Mk 14:11, Lk 15:5, 3219:6, 3722:523:8, Jo 4:368:5620:20, Ac 5:418:3911:2313:48, II Co 6:107:713:9, Phl 2:17, 28, Col 2:5, I Th 5:16, I Pe 4:13, III Jo 3; χ. καὶ ἀγαλλιᾶσθαι, Mt 5:12; κ. σκιρτᾶν, Lk 6:23; opp. to κλαίειν, Ro 12:15, I Co 7:30; to κλαίειν κ. θρηνεῖνJo 16:20; to λύπην ἔχειν, ib. 22; c. cogn. acc, χ. χαρὰν μεγάλην, Mt 2:10; χαρᾷ χ. (B1., § 38, 3; Dalman, Words, 34 f.), Jo 3:29; ἡ χαρὰ ᾗ χαίρομεν, I Th 3:9; c. prep. (Bl., § 38, 2), ἐπί, c. dat. (simple dat. in cl.), Mt 18:13, Lk 1:1413:17, Ac 15:31, Ro 16:19, I Co 13:616:17, II Co 7:13, Re 11:10; διά, Jo 3:2911:15, I Th 3:9; ἐν, Phl 1:18; ἀπό, II Co 2:3; c. acc. (Dem.), Phl 2:18; seq. ὅτι, Jo 14:28, II Co 7:9, 16, II Jo 4; ἐν τούτῳ ὅτι, Lk 10:20; c. dat., Ro 12:1; ἐν κυρίῳ, Phl 4:10
2. In salutations, imperat., χαῖρε, χαίρετε,
(a) at meeting, hail: Mt 26:4927:29, Mk 15:18, Lk 1:28, Jo 19:3; pl., Mt 28:9; so χαίρειν λέγω, to give greeting, II Jo 11; in letters, χαίρειν (sc. λέγει; Bl., § 81, 1), greeting: Ac 15:2323:26Ja 1:1;
(b) at parting, farewell: II Co 13:11;
(c) on other occasions, be of good cheer: ἐν κυρίῳ, Phl 3:14:4 (cf. συν-χαίρω).†

χαρά.long: joy, gladness, a source of joy.
χαρά.kj: gladness, X greatly, (X be exceeding) joy(-ful, -fully, -fulness, -ous)
χαρά.as:
χαρά, -ᾶς, ἡ
(< χαίρω), [in LXX for שִׂמְחָה, שָׂשׂוֹן, etc. ;]
joy, delight: Lk 1:1415:7, 10, Jo 15:1116:22, 2417:13, Ac 8:8, II Co 1:247:138:2, Ga 5:22, Col 1:11, Phl 2:2, I Jo 1:4, II Jo 12; opp. to κατήφεια, Ja 4:9; to λύπη, Jo 16:20; χ. τῆς πίστεως, Phl 1:25; ἀγαλλιᾶσθαι (χαίρειν, q.v.), χαρᾷ, Jo 3:29, I Pe 1:8; χ. ἔχειν, Phm 7; πληροῦν (-οῦσθαι) χαρᾶς, Ac 13:52, Ro 15:13, II Ti 1:4; ποιεῖν χ. μεγάλην, Ac 15:3; ἀπὸ τῆς χ., Mt 13:44, Lk 24:41, Ac 12:14; ἐν χ., Ro 15:32; μετὰ χαρᾶς, Mt 13:2028:8, Mk 4:16, Lk 8:1310:1724:52, Phl 1:42:29, He 10:3413:17; id. seq.πνεύματος ἁγίου, I Th 1:6; χ. ἐν π. ἁ, Ro 14:17; χ. ἐπί, II Co 7:4; διά, I Th 3:9; ὅτι, Jo 16:21; ἵνα, III Jo 4 By meton., of the cause or occasion of joy: Lk 2:10, II Co 1:15, WH, txt., R, mg., Phl 4:1, I Th 2:19, 20, He 12:2, Ja 1:2; ἡ χ. τ. κυρίου, Mt 25:21, 23.†

χρυσός.long: gold, anything made of gold, a gold coin.
χρυσός.sd: gold; by extension, a golden article, as an ornament or coin
χρυσός.der: perhaps from the base of G5530 (χράομαι) (through the idea of the utility of the metal);
χρυσός.as:
χρυσός, -οῦ, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for זהב ;]
gold: Mt 2:11, Re 9:7; of golden ornaments, Mt 23:16, 17, I Ti 2:9 (Rec., WH, mg.), Ja 5:3, Re 17:4 (Rec., WH, mg.) Re 18:12, 16 (Rec., WH, mg.); of images, Ac 17:29; of gold coin, Mt 10:9.†

χρηματίζω.long: (originally: I transact business), (a) act. of God: I warn; pass: I am warned by God (probably in response to an inquiry as to one's duty), (b) (I take a name from my public business, hence) I receive a name, am publicly called.
χρηματίζω.sd: to utter an oracle (compare the original sense of G5530 (χράομαι)), i.e. divinely intimate; by implication, (compare the secular sense of G5532 (χρεία)) to constitute a firm for business, i.e. (generally) bear as a title
χρηματίζω.kj: be called, be admonished (warned) of God, reveal, speak
χρηματίζω.as:
χρηματίζω
(< χρῆμα), [in LXX: Je 33 (26):236 (29):2337 (30):243 (36):2, 4 A (דּבר pi.), 32:16 (25:30) (שׁאג), III Ki 18:27, Jb 40:3 (8) * ;]
1.to transact business, hence, to consult, deliberate (Thuc., Dem., al.); hence in later writers,
2.to make answer (esp. of offcial pronounce­ments by magistrates, etc.; in π. of the royal reply to an ἔντευξις, q.v.; cf. Deiss., BS, 122); of an answer by an oracle (Diod., Plut., al.); in FlJ, LXX and NT, of divine communications, to instruct, admonish, warn: pass. (Bl., § 54, 3), Mt 2:22, He 8:511:712:25; c. inf. (Bl., § 69,4; 70, 3; 72, 5), Mt 2:12, Lk 2:26, Ac 10:22
3.to assume a name (as in business), be called (Polyb., al.): Ac 11:26, Ro 7:3 (gnomic fut.; cf. Burton, § 69).†

χώρα.long: (a) a country or region, (b) the land, as opposed to the sea, (c) the country, distinct from town, (d) plur: fields.
χώρα.sd: room, i.e. a space of territory (more or less extensive; often including its inhabitants)
χώρα.kj: coast, county, fields, ground, land, region
χώρα.der: feminine of a derivative of the base of G5490 (χάσμα) through the idea of empty expanse;
χώρα.as:
χώρα, -ας, ἡ
[in LXX for אֶרֶץ, מְדִינָה, etc. ;]
1. most freq. in cl., a space, place.
2.land, i.e.
(a)a land, country, region: Mt 12:2, Mk 5:106:55, Lk 2:815:13-1519:12, Jo 11:54, Ac 13:4927:27; χ. Γαλατική, Ac 16:618:23; Τραχωνίτιδος, Lk 3:1; τ. Ἰουδαίας, Ac 26:20; τ. Ἰουδαίων, Ac 10:39; pl., τῆς Ἰουδαίας κ. Σαμαρείας, Ac 8:1; Γεργεσηνῶν (Γερασηνῶν, Γαδαρηνῶν) Mt 8:28, Mk 5:1, Lk 8:26; ἐν χ. καὶ σκιᾷ θανάτου, Mt 4:16;
(b)land, property: Lk 12:16;
(c)the country, opp. to the town; so in pl., Lk 21:21, Jo 4:35, Ja 5:4.†
SYN.: ἄγρος, τόπος (cf. DCG, i, 591a; LS, s.v. χώρα, ad init.).

χείρ.sd: the hand (literally or figuratively (power); especially (by Hebraism) a means or instrument)
χείρ.der: perhaps from the base of G5494 (χειμών) in the sense of its congener the base of G5490 (χάσμα) (through the idea of hollowness for grasping);
χείρ.as:
χείρ, gen., χειρος (acc., χεῖραν, I Pe 5:6 T), ἡ,
[in LXX chiefly for יָד ;]
the hand: Mt 3:12, Mk 3:1, Lk 6:6, al. mult.; ἡ χ., acting subject, Lk 22:21; pl., Ac 17:2520:34, I Jo 1:1; τ. ἔργα τῶν χ., Ac 7:41, Re 9:20; ὁ ἀσπασμὸς τ. ἐμῇ χ., I Co 16:21, Col 4:18, II Th 3:17; prepositional phrases, esp. those without art., similar to Heb. constructions (Bl., §32, 4; 40, 9; 46, 9), ἐν χ.; c gen. (Lft., in l.), Ga 3:19; σὺν χ. ἀγγέλου, Ac 7:35; διὰ (τῶν) χειρῶν (διὰ χειρός), Mk 6:2, Ac 5:127:25, al.; ἐπὶ χειρῶν, Mt 4:6, Lk 4:11; ellipse of χ. (ἡ δεξία, ἀριστερα; Bl., § 44, 1), Mt 6:3, al. By meton., for the power or activity of an individual, Mt 17:22, Mk 9:31, Lk 9:44, Jo 10:39, Ac 12:11, al.; metaph., of the activity or power of God: Lk 1:6623:46, Jo 10:29, Ac 11:2113:11, al.

χρεία.sd: employment, i.e. an affair; also (by implication) occasion, demand, requirement or destitution
χρεία.kj: business, lack, necessary(-ity), need(-ful), use, want
χρεία.der: from the base of G5530 (χράομαι) or G5534 (χρή);
χρεία.as:
χρεία, -ας, ἡ
[in LXX: II Ch 2:16 (15) (צֹרֶךְ), II Es 7:20 (חַשְׁחוּת) freq. in Si, I-II Mac ;]
1.need, necessity: Ac 28:10, Tit 3:14; πρὸς οἰκοδομὴν τῆς χ. (RV, txt., for edifying as the need may be; but v. Field, Notes, 192), Eph 4:29; ἕστι χ., Lk 10:42, He 7:11; χ. ἔχειν, c. gen., Mt 6:821:3, Mk 11:3, Lk 9:1115:719:31, 3422:71, Jo 13:29, I Co 12:21, 24, I Th 4:12, He 10:36, Re 21:2322:5; seq. τοῦ, c. inf. (Bl., § 71, 3), He 5:12; absol. (sc. gen.), Ac 2:454:35; c. gen. pers., Mt 9:1226:65, Mk 2:1714:63, Lk 5:31; c. inf. (Bl., § 69, 5), Mt 3:1414:16, Jo 13:10 , I Th 1:84:9; seq. ἵνα, Jo 2:2516:30, I Jo 2:27; absol., Mk 2:25, Eph 4:28, I Jo 3:17; οὐδὲν χ. ἔχειν, Re 3:17; ἡ χ., c. gen. subjc., Phl 2:254:16, 19; pl., Ac 20:34, Ro 12:13.
2.matter, business (so esp. in late writers, Polyb., al.; I Mac 12:45, al.): Ac 6:3.†

χορτάζω.sd: to fodder, i.e. (generally) to gorge (supply food in abundance)
χορτάζω.as:
χορτάζω
(< χόρτος), [in LXX for שׂבע, Ps 16 (17):14 al. ;]
(a) prop., of animals (v. Lft. on Phl 4:12), to feed, fatten: Re 19:21;
(b) in late Gk. (Kennedy, Sources, 82, 156), of persons, to fill or satisfy with food: c. acc. pers., Mt 15:33; pass., Mt 14:2015:37, Mk 6:427:278:8, Lk 9:17, Jo 6:26, Ja 2:16; opp. to πεινᾶν, Phl 4:12; c. gen. rei, Mk 8:4; ἀπό, Lk 16:21; ἐκ, Lk 15:16, WH, txt.,; metaph., Mt 5:6, Lk 6:21.†

χιτών.as:
χιτών, ῶνος, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for כְּתֹנֶת:]
the garment worn next the skin (though two tunics were sometimes worn, v. Swete, Mk., 117), a tunic: Mt 10:10, Mk 6:914:63, Lk 3:119:3, Ju 23; disting. from ἱμάτιον (q.v.), Mt 5:40, Lk 6:29, Jo 19:23, Ac 9:39 (v. DCG, i, 338a, 340a, 499a)

χόρτος.sd: a "court" or "garden", i.e. (by implication, of pasture) herbage or vegetation
χόρτος.as:
χόρτος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for עֶשֶׂב, also for חָצִיר, etc. ;]
1.an enclosure, a feeding place (Hom.).
2.food, esp. for cattle, grass: Mt 13:2614:19, Mk 4:286:39, Lk 12:28, Jo 6:10, I Co 3:12, Ja 1:10, 11, I Pe 1:24(LXX), Re 9:4; χ. χλωρός, Mk 6:39, Re 8:7.†

χρῄζω.long: I need, have need of, want, desire.
χρῄζω.sd: to make (i.e. have) necessity, i.e. be in want of
χρῄζω.as:
χρῄζω
(< χρή) [in LXX Jg 11:7, I Ki 17:18 A * ;]
to need, have need of: c. gen. rei, Mt 6:32, Lk 11:812:30, II Co 3:1; c. gen. pers. seq. ἐν, Ro 16:2.†

χοῖρος.as:
** χοῖρος, -ου, ὁ
[in Sm.: Is 65:466:3 ;]
a swine: pl., Mt 7:68:30-32, Mk 5:11-13, 16, Lk 8:32, 3315:15, 16 †

χαλεπός.sd: difficult, i.e. dangerous, or (by implication) furious
χαλεπός.der: perhaps from G5465 (χαλάω) through the idea of reducing the strength;
χαλεπός.as:
χαλεπός, -ή, -όν
[in LXX: Is 18:2 (נוֺרָא), Wi 3:19, Si 3:21, al. ;]
hard;
(a)hard to do or deal with, difficult;
(b)hard to bear, painful, grievous: καιροί, II Ti 3:1;
(c) of persons, hard to deal with, harsh, fierce, savage: Mt 8:28.†

χείρων.sd: from an obsolete equivalent (of uncertain derivation); more evil or aggravated (physically, mentally or morally)
χείρων.as:
χείρων, -ον, compar. of κακός
[in LXX: I Ki 17:43 B, Wi 15:1817:6, III Mac 5:20 * ;]
worse: Mt 9:1612:4527:64, Mk 2:21, Lk 11:26, Jo 5:14, I Ti 5:8, He 10:29, II Pe 2:20; εἰς (ἐπὶ) τὸ χεῖρον, Mk 5:26, II Ti 3:13.†

χαλκός.long: copper, brass, money; a brazen musical instrument.
χαλκός.sd: copper (the substance, or some implement or coin made of it)
χαλκός.der: perhaps from G5465 (χαλάω) through the idea of hollowing out as a vessel (this metal being chiefly used for that purpose);
χαλκός.as:
χαλκός, -οῦ, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for נְחֹשֶׁת ;]
copper: I Co 13:1, Re 18:12; by meton., of copper coin, Mt 10:9, Mk 6:812:41.†

χωλός.long: lame, deprived of a foot, limping.
χωλός.as:
χωλός, -ή, -όν
[in LXX for פִּסֵּחַ ;]
lame, halt, maimed: Mt 11:515:30, 3118:821:14, Mk 9:45, Lk 7:2214:13, 21, Jo 5:3, Ac 3:28:714:8, He 12:13.†

Χοραζίν.as:
Χοραζείν (Rec. -ζίν), ἡ,
Chorazin, a town of Galilee: Mt 11:21, Lk 10:13.†

χρηστός.sd: employed, i.e. (by implication) useful (in manner or morals)
χρηστός.as:
χρηστός, -ή, -όν
(< χράομαι), [in LXX chiefly for טוֹב (freq. of God: Ps 24 (25):8, al.), also for יָקָר (Ez 27:2228:13), יָשָׁר (Pr 2:21א A) ;]
serviceable, good;
(a) of things, good, pleasant: of food (as often in cl.), οἶνος, Lk 5:39; ζυγός, Mt 11:30 (EV, easy); in ethical sense, ἤθη, I Co 15:33;
(b) of persons, good, kind, gracious: Eph 4:32; of God, Lk 6:35, I Pe 2:3; τ. χρηστὸν (= ἡ χρηστότης) τοῦ θεοῦ, Ro 2:4.†

χωρίς.sd: at a space, i.e. separately or apart from (often as preposition)
χωρίς.as:
χωρίς
adv.,
1.separately, apart: Jo 20:7.
2. As prep., c. gen.,
(a)separate from, apart from, without (practically equiv. to ἄνευ; v. Field, Notes, 103): Mt 13:34, Mk 4:34, Lk 6:49, Jo 1:315:5, Ro 3:21, 284:67:8, 910:14, I Co 4:811:11, II Co 12:3, Eph 2:12, Phl 2:14, I Ti 2:85:21, Phm 14, He 4:157:7, 209:7, 189:22, 2810:2811:6, 4012:8, 14 (οὗ χωρίς; v. Bl., § 82, 3), Ja 2:18, 20, 26;
(b)besides: Mt 14:2115:38, II Co 11:28.†

χεῖλος.long: a lip, mouth, shore, edge, brink; meton: language, dialect.
χεῖλος.sd: a lip (as a pouring place); figuratively, a margin (of water)
χεῖλος.der: from a form of the same as G5490 (χάσμα);
χεῖλος.as:
χεῖλος, -ους, τό, gen. pl., -εων (v. Bl., § 8, 4; Thackeray, Gr., I, 151),
[in LXX chiefly for שָׂפָה ;]
a lip (as in Heb., of the lip as the organ of speech): Mt 15:8, Mk 7:6, Ro 3:13, I Co 14:21, He 13:15, I Pe 3:10(LXX). Metaph., of things, an edge, brink, etc. (Hom., Hdt., al.): of the sea­shore, He 11:12.†

χωρέω.long: (lit: I make room, hence) (a) I have room for, receive, contain, (b) I make room for by departing, go, make progress, turn myself.
χωρέω.sd: to be in (give) space, i.e. (intransitively) to pass, enter, or (transitively) to hold, admit (literally or figuratively)
χωρέω.kj: come, contain, go, have place, (can, be room to) receive
χωρέω.as:
χωρέω, -ῶ
[in LXX: Ge 13:6 (נשׂא), III Ki 7:26, 38 (כּוּל hi.), II Ch 4:5 (חזק hi.), Wi 7:23, 24, al. ;]
I. Intrans.,
1.to make room, give way, retire, pass: seq. εἰς, Mt 15:17; metaph. (EV, come), εἰς μετάνοιαν, II Pe 3:9.
2.to go forward, advance, progress (Plat., Polyb., al.) ὁ λόγος ὁ ἐμὸς οὐ χωρεῖ. ἐν ὑμῖν, Jo 8:37 (R, txt., hath not free course; R, mg., hath no place, for wh. cf. Field, Notes, 94 f.).
II. Trans., to have space for holding, to hold: Mk 2:2 (cf. Ge, l.c.), Jo 21:25; of measures (III Ki, II Ch, ll. c.), Jo 2:6. Metaph., of having or making room in mind or heart: Mt 19:11, 12 (EV, receive), II Co 7:2 (R, txt., open your hearts; mg., make room) (cf. ἀνα-, ἀπο-, ἐκ-, ὑπο-χωρέω).†

Χαναναῖος.long: Canaanite, a Biblical and archaic name for Phoenician.
Χαναναῖος.sd: a Chanaanæan (i.e. Kenaanite), or native of gentile Palestine

χειμών.long: a storm, tempest; winter, the rainy season.
χειμών.sd: akin to the base of 5490 through the idea of a channel), meaning a storm (as pouring rain); by implication, the rainy season, i.e. winter
χειμών.as:
χειμών, -ῶνος, ὁ
[in LXX for גֶּשֶׁם, סְתָיו ;]
1.winter: Jo 10:22, II Ti 4:21; gen., χειμῶνος, in winter, Mt 24:20, Mk 13:18.
2. Prop., a winter storm, hence, generally, a storm, tempest: Mt 16:3 (T, WH, R, mg., om.), Ac 27:20.†

χωρίζω.long: (a) I separate, put apart, (b) mid. or pass: I separate myself, depart, withdraw.
χωρίζω.sd: to place room between, i.e. part; reflexively, to go away
χωρίζω.as:
χωρίζω
[in LXX: II Ch 12:8, al. (בּדל ni., etc.), Wi 1:3, II Mac 5:21, al. ;]
1.to separate, divide, put asunder: c. acc. rei, opp. to συζεύγνυμιMt 19:6, Mk 10:9; c. acc. pers., seq. ἀπό (Wi 1:3), Ro 8:35, 39; pf. pass ptcp., He 7:26.
2. In late writers, mid. and 1 aor pass., to separate oneself, depart: Phm 15; seq. ἀπόAc 1:4, ἐκ, Ac 18:1-2; of divorce (polyb., al.), I Co 7:10, 11, 15 (cf. ἀπο-, δια-χωρίζω).†

χρονίζω.long: I delay, tarry, linger, spend time.
χρονίζω.as:
χρονίζω
(< χρόνος), [in LXX chiefly for אחר pi. ;]
to spend or take time, to tarry, linger, delay: Mt 24:4825:5, He 10:37; seq. ἐν, c. dat. loc., Lk 1:21; c. inf., Lk 12:45.†

χωρίον.g: a place, piece of land, field
χωρίον.long: a place, piece of land, field, property, estate.
χωρίον.sd: a spot or plot of ground
χωρίον.kj: field, land, parcel of ground, place, possession
χωρίον.as:
χωρίον, -ου, τό
(dimin. of χώρα, χῶρος), [in LXX: I Ch 27:27 (כֶּרֶם), II Mac 11:512:7, 21, IV Mac 15:20 * ;]
1.a place, region.
2.an estate, property, piece of land: Mt 26:36, Mk 14:32, Jo 4:5, Ac 1:18, 194:345:3, 828:7.†

χλαμύς.long: a short cloak, worn by military officers and soldiers.
χλαμύς.as:
* χλαμύς, -ύδος, ἡ
[in LXX: II Mac 12:35 * ;]
a chlamys, or short cloak worn over the χιτών (q.v.): Mt 27:28, 31 (v. Tr., Syn., § 1).†

χολή.sd: "gall" or bile, i.e. (by analogy) poison or an anodyne (wormwood, poppy, etc.)
χολή.der: feminine of an equivalent perhaps akin to the same as 5514 (from the greenish hue);
χολή.as:
χολή, -ῆς, ἡ
[in LXX for רֹאשׁ, לַעֲנָה, מְרֵרָה ;]
gall: Mt 27:34 (here prob. = myrrh, cf. Mk 15:23, v. Swete, in l.; DCG, i, 634a); metaph., Ac 8:23.†

χιών.der: perhaps akin to the base of G5490 (χάσμα) (G5465 (χαλάω)) or G5494 (χειμών) (as descending or empty);
χιών.as:
χιών, -όνος, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for שֶׁלֶג also (in Da) for תְּלַג ;]
snow: Mt 28:3, Re 1:14.†

χαλάω.long: I let down, lower, slacken, loosen.
χαλάω.as:
χαλάω, -ῶ
[in LXX: (Je 45 (38):6) (שׁלח pi.), etc. ;]
(a)to slacken, loosen;
(b)to let loose, let go;
(c)to lower, let down: c. acc. rei, Mk 2:4, Lk 5:4, 5, Ac 9:2527:17, 30; c. acc. pers. (cf. Je, l.c.), pass., II Co 11:33.†

χοῦς.sd: a heap (as poured out), i.e. rubbish; loose dirt
χοῦς.as:
χοῦς, -οός acc., οῦν, ὁ, (contr. from χόος),
[in LXX chiefly for עָפָר ;]
1.earth, soil.
2. In later writers (Plut., LXX), = κονιορτός, dust: Mk 6:11, Re 18:19.†

χιλίαρχος.long: a commander of a thousand men, a military tribune.
χιλίαρχος.sd: the commander of a thousand soldiers ("chiliarch"; i.e. colonel
χιλίαρχος.as:
χιλίαρχος (in Hdt., al., -ης), -ου, ὁ
(< χίλιοι, ἄρχω) [in LXX chiefly for אֶלֶףשַׂר ;]
a chiliarch, the commander of a thousand, esp. a Roman military tribune, the commander of a cohort: Jo 18:12, Ac 21:31-33, 3722:24-2923:10, 15, 17-19, 2224:7, 2225:23; more generally, of officers of similar rank, Mk 6:21, Re 6:1519:18 (v., DB, i, 352b; DCG, i, 271a, 307a).†

χλωρός.as:
χλωρός, -ά, -όν
(< χλόη), [in LXX for יֶרֶק, etc. ;]
(a)pale green: χόρτος, Mk 6:39, Re 8:7; πᾶν χ., Re 9:4;
(b)pale: ἵππος, Re 6:8.†

χαλκίον.as:
χαλκίον, -ου, τό
(< χαλκός), [in LXX: Jb 41:22(23) (סִיר), etc. ;]
a brazen (copper) vessel: Mk 7:4.†

χρῆμα.sd: something useful or needed, i.e. wealth, price
χρῆμα.as:
χρῆμα, -τος, τό
(< χράομαι) [in LXX: Jos 22:8, II Ch 1:11, 12 (נְכָסׅים), Jb 27:17 (כֶּסֶף), etc.; freq. in (Si (5:1, 8, al.), II and IV Mac ;]
a thing that one uses or needs (and generally, a matter, event, business); hence in pl.,
(a)wealth, riches: οἱ τά χ. ἔχοντες, Mk 10:23, 24, Lk 18:24;
(b)money: Ac 8:18, 2024:26; sing. (rare in cl.) of a special sum of money, Ac 4:37.†

χήρα.sd: a widow (as lacking a husband), literally or figuratively
χήρα.der: feminine of a presumed derivative apparently from the base of G5490 (χάσμα) through the idea of deficiency;
χήρα.as:
χήρα, -ας, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for אַלְמָנָה ;]
a widow: Mt 23:13 (Rec., R, mg.), Mk 12:40-43, Lk 2:374:257:1218:3, 520:4721:2, 3, Ac 6:19:39, 41, I Co 7:8, I Ti 5:3-5, 11, 16, Ja 1:27; γυνὴ χ., Lk 4:26; of one of an ordo viduarum (v. CGT, in l.), I Ti 5:9; metaph., of a city forsaken, Re 18:7.†

χειροποίητος.long: done or made with hands, artificial.
χειροποίητος.der: from G5495 (χείρ) and a derivative of G4160 (ποιέω);
χειροποίητος.as:
χειρο-ποίητος, -ον
(< χείρ, ποιέω), [in LXX (of idols) for אֱלִיל ;]
made by hand (i.e. of human handiwork): of temples, Mk 14:58, Ac 7:4817:24, He 9:11, 24; of circumcision, Eph 2:11.†

χαριτόω.sd: to grace, i.e. indue with special honor
χαριτόω.as:
† χαριτόω, -ῶ
(< χάρις), [in LXX: Si 18:17 (ἀνδρί κεχαριτωμένῳ; Vg., justificato; Syr., saintly) * ;]
to endow withχάρις (q.v.), i.e.
1. (a) to make graceful;
(b)to make gracious (Si, l.c.).
2. In Hellenistic writings (for exx., v. AR, Eph., 227; Lft., Notes, 315),
(a)to cause to find favour;
(b)to endue with grace (i.e. divine favour): Lk 1:28, Eph 1:6.†

χάρις.long: (a) grace, as a gift or blessing brought to man by Jesus Christ, (b) favor, (c) gratitude, thanks, (d) a favor, kindness.
χάρις.sd: graciousness (as gratifying), of manner or act (abstract or concrete; literal, figurative or spiritual; especially the divine influence upon the heart, and its reflection in the life; including gratitude)
χάρις.kj: acceptable, benefit, favour, gift, grace(- ious), joy, liberality, pleasure, thank(-s, -worthy)
χάρις.as:
χάρις, -ιτος, ἡ Abbott-Smith does not include the article here., acc., χάριν (χάριτα in Ac 24:27, Ju 4; v. WH, App., 157),
[in LXX chiefly for חֵן ;]
1. objectively, that which causes favourable regard, gracefulness, grace, loveliness of form, graciousness of speech (cl.; Ec 10:12, Si 21:16, al.): Col 4:6; λόγοι τ. χάριτος (gen. qual.), Lk 4:22.
2. Subjectively,
(a) on the part of the giver, grace, graciousness, kindness, goodwill, favour: Lk 2:52, Ac 7:10, al.; esp. in NT of the divine favour, grace, with emphasis on its freeness and universality: Lk 1:30, Ac 14:26, Ro 1:7, I Co 1:3, al.; opp. to ὀφείλημα, Ro 4:4, 16; to ἔργα, Ro 11:6;
(b) on the part of the receiver, a sense of favour received, thanks, gratitude: Ro 6:177:25, al.; χ. ἔχειν, to be thankful, Lk 17:9, I Ti 1:12, al.
3. Objectively, of the effect of grace,
(a) a state of grace: Ro 5:2, II Ti 2:1, I Pe 5:12, II Pe 3:18;
(b) a proof or gift of grace (cl., a favour): Jo 1:16, Ac 6:8, Ro 1:5, I Co 3:10, II Co 9:8, Ga 2:9, Eph 3:2, I Pe 5:5, 10 al. (For fuller treatment of the NT usage, v. AR, Eph., 221 ff.; DB, ii, 254 ff.; DCG, i, 686 ff.; Cremer, s.v.).

χρίω.sd: to smear or rub with oil, i.e. (by implication) to consecrate to an office or religious service
χρίω.der: probably akin to G5530 (χράομαι) through the idea of contact;
χρίω.as:
χρίω
to anoint (Hom., al.);
[in LXX chiefly for משׁח of consecration to a sacred office: priest, Ex 28:41; prophet, III Ki 19:16; king, I Ki 10:1; of things, Ex 40:9, Le 8:10, al.].
In NT, metaph., of God's anointing,
(a) Christ: Ac 4:27; c. inf., Lk 4:18(LXX); c. dupl. acc (v. Bl., § 34, 4), He 1:9(LXX); πνεύματι ἁγίῳ, Ac 10:38;
(b) Christians: II Co 1:21 (cf. Westc., Epp. Jo., 73) (cf. ἐν-, ἐπι-Χριω).†
SYN: v.s. ἀλείφω

χαρίζομαι.long: (a) I show favor to, (b) I pardon, forgive, (c) I show kindness.
χαρίζομαι.sd: to grant as a favor, i.e. gratuitously, in kindness, pardon or rescue
χαρίζομαι.as:
χαρίζομαι
(< χάρις), [in LXX: Es 8:7 (נתן), Ca 1:4א, Si 12:3, II-IV Mac 9 * ;]
1.to show favour or kindness: c. dat. pers., Ga 3:18.
2.to give freely, bestow: c. acc et dat., Lk 7:21, Ac 3:1425:11, 1627:24, Ro 8:32, I Co 2:12, Phl 1:292:9, Phm 22.
3. In late Gk. (= Lat. condonare), to grant forgiveness, forgive freely: of debt, Lk 7:42, 43 (EGT, in l.); of sin, II Co 2:7, 1012:13, Eph 4:32, Col 2:133:13 (cf. DB, ii, 57a).†

χρεοφειλέτης.der: from a derivative of G5531 (χράω) and G3781 (ὀφειλέτης);
χρεοφειλέτης.as:
† χρεοφειλέτης (Rec. χρεω-, WH, χρεοφιλ-; v. WH, App., 152, 154), -ου, ὁ,
(< χρέος, a debt, + ὀφειλέτης) [in LXX: Jb 31:37, Pr 29:13 * ;]
a debtor: Lk 7:4116:5.†

χάριν.long: for the sake of, by reason of, on account of.
χάριν.sd: through favor of, i.e. on account of
χάριν.kj: be-(for) cause of, for sake of, +…fore, X reproachfully
χάριν.der: accusative case of G5485 (χάρις) as preposition;

Χουζᾶς.long: Chuza, a steward of Herod Antipas.

χιλιάς.long: a thousand, the number one thousand.
χιλιάς.as:
χιλιάς, -άδος, ἡ
(< χίλιοι), [in LXX for אֶלֶף ;]
the number one thousand, a thousand: Lk 14:31, Ac 4:4, I Co 10:8, Re 5:117:4-811:1314:1, 321:16.†

χορός.as:
χορός, -οῦ, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for מָחוֹל, מְחֹלָה ;]
a dance: pl., Lk 15:26.†

χάσμα.der: from a form of an obsolete primary (to "gape" or "yawn");
χάσμα.as:
χάσμα, -τος, τό
(< χάσκω, to yawn), [in LXX: II Ki 18:17 (פַּחַת)* ;]
a chasm, wide space: Lk 16:26.†

χάραξ.sd: akin to G1125 (γράφω) through the idea of scratching); a stake, i.e. (by implication) a palisade or rampart (military mound for circumvallation in a siege)
χάραξ.as:
χάραξ, -ακος, ὁ
(< χαράσσω), [in LXX for סֹלְלָה, מָצוֹר, etc. ;]
1.a pointed stake
2.a palisade or rampart: Lk 19:43.†

χολάω.sd: to be bilious, i.e. (by implication) irritable (enraged, "choleric")
χολάω.as:
** χολάω, -ῶ
(< χολή), [in LXX: III Mac 3:1 R * ;]
1.to be melancholy mad (Aristoph.).
2. = χολοῦμαι, to be angry: c. dat. pers., Jo 7:23.†

χαμαί.der: adverb perhaps from the base of G5490 (χάσμα) through the idea of a fissure in the soil;

χείμαρρος.der: from the base of G5494 (χειμών) and G4482 (ῥέω);
χείμαρρος.as:
χείμμαρος (shortened form of the more usual -οος, Attic contr., -ους), -ον
(< χεῖμα, ῥέω) [in LXX chiefly for נַחַל ;]
winter-flowing; as subst., ὁ χ. (sc. ποταμός), a torrent: Jo 18:1.†

χρυσίον.long: a piece of gold, golden ornament.
χρυσίον.sd: a golden article, i.e. gold plating, ornament, or coin
χρυσίον.as:
χρυσίον, -ου, τό
(dimin. of χρυσός, q.v.), [in LXX chiefly for זָהָב ;]
a piece of gold, gold: I Co 3:12, He 9:4, I Pe 1:7, Re 3:1821:18, 21; of golden ornaments, I Ti 2:9 (WH, txt., RV), I Pe 3:3, Re 17:418:16 (WH, txt., R); of gold coin, money, Ac 3:620:33, I Pe 1:18.†

Χαρράν.sd: Charrhan (i.e. Charan), a place in Mesopotamia
Χαρράν.as:
Χαρράν
indecl. (in FlJ., Ant., i, 16, 1, Κάρρα, -ας, ib. 6, 5, Χαρρά, -ᾶς; so LXX: Ge 29:4 E, Ez 27:28 B, elsewhere -άν—Heb. חָרָן), Haran, a town in N.W. Mesopotamia: Ac 7:2, 4.†

Χαλδαῖος.sd: a Chaldæan (i.e. Kasdi), or native or the region of the lower Euphrates
Χαλδαῖος.as:
Χαλδαῖος, -ου, ὁ
a Chaldæan: γῆ Χαλδαίων, Ac 7:4.†

Χανάαν.long: Canaan, the whole of Palestine or Palestine west of the river Jordan.
Χανάαν.sd: Chanaan (i.e. Kenaan), the early name of Palestine
Χανάαν.as:
Χαναάν, ἡ indecl. (Heb. כְּנַעַן),
Canaan: Ac 7:11; γῆ Χ., Ac 13:19.†

χόρτασμα.as:
† χόρτασμα, -τος, τό
(< χορτάζω), [in LXX: Ge 24:25, 3242:2743:24, Jg 19:19 (מִסְפּוֹא), De 11:16 (עֶשֶׂב), (Si 30:33 (33:24)) Si 38:26 * ;]
fodder (Polyb., Plut., al.): pl., Ac 7:11 (RV, sustenance).†

χειραγωγέω.sd: to be a hand-leader, i.e. to guide (a blind person)
χειραγωγέω.as:
χειραγωγέω, -ῶ
(< χειραγωγός), [in LXX: Jg 16:26 A (בְּיָרמַחֲזׅיק), To 11:16א * ;]
to lead by the hand: Ac 9:822:11.†

Χριστιανός.sd: a Christian, i.e. follower of Christ
Χριστιανός.as:
Χριστιανός (D, Χρεισ-; on the form Χρησ-, v. Bl., § 3, 6; 27, 4 on the ending, -ανος, v. Bl., ll. c.; Deiss., LAE, 382), -οῦ ὁ,
a Christian, the name first given to the disciples by pagan gentiles at Antioch: Ac 11:2626:28, I Pe 4:16 (v. reff. in Thayer, s.v.; also DB, i, 384).†

χειραγωγός.g: one who leads a helpless person by the hand
χειραγωγός.long: one who leads a helpless person by the hand.
χειραγωγός.sd: a hand-leader, i.e. personal conductor (of a blind person)
χειραγωγός.kj: some to lead by the hand
χειραγωγός.der: from G5495 (χείρ) and a reduplicated form of G71 (ἄγω);
χειραγωγός.as:
* χειρ-αγωγός, -όν
(< χείρ, ἄγω)
leading by the hand. As subst., ὁ χ., one to lead by the head, a guide: Ac 13:11.†

χειροτονέω.long: I elect by show of hands, choose by vote, appoint.
χειροτονέω.sd: to be a hand-reacher or voter (by raising the hand), i.e. (generally) to select or appoint
χειροτονέω.der: from a comparative of G5495 (χείρ) and (to stretch);
χειροτονέω.as:
* χειρο-τονέω, -ῶ
(< χείρ, τείνω)
1.to vote by stretching out the hand in the Athenian ἐκκλησία (Luc., Plut.).
2.to appoint:
(a) by vote, II Co 8:19
(b) without vote, Ac 14:23 (v. Rackham, in l.) (cf. προχειροτονέω).†

χάραγμα.sd: a scratch or etching, i.e. stamp (as a badge of servitude), or scupltured figure (statue)
χάραγμα.as:
* χάραγμα, -τος, τό
(< χαράσσω, to engrave),
(a)a stamp, impress, mark: Re 13:16, 1714:9, 1116:219:2020:4 (v. Deiss., BS, 240 ff.);
(b)a thing graven: Ac 17:29.†

χλευάζω.sd: to throw out the lip, i.e. jeer at
χλευάζω.der: from a derivative probably of G5491 (χεῖλος);
χλευάζω.as:
* χλευάζω
(< χλεύη, a jest), [in LXX: Wi 11:14, II Mac 7:7, IV Mac 5:22 * ;]
to jest, mock, jeer: Ac 17:32.†

χρώς.long: the skin, surface of the body.
χρώς.sd: the body (properly, its surface or skin)
χρώς.der: probably akin to the base of G5530 (χράομαι) through the idea of handling;
χρώς.as:
χρώς, gen., χρωτός, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for בָּשָׂר ;]
in cl. rare in prose, the surface of the body, skin: Ac 19:12.†

Χίος.long: Chios (modern Scio), an important island in the Aegean Sea, off the west central coast of Asia Minor.
Χίος.sd: Chios, an island in the Mediterranean
Χίος.as:
Χίος, -ου, ἡ
Chios, an island in Ægean Sea: Ac 20:15.†

χρονοτριβέω.long: I waste time, spend time, delay.
χρονοτριβέω.sd: to be a time-wearer, i.e. to procrastinate (linger)
χρονοτριβέω.der: from a presumed compound of G5550 (χρόνος) and the base of G5147 (τρίβος);
χρονοτριβέω.as:
* χρονοτριβέω, -ῶ
(< χρόνος, τρίβω),
to spend time: Ac 20:16.†

χράομαι.g: I use, make use of, deal with
χράομαι.long: I use, make use of, deal with, take advantage of.
χράομαι.sd: to furnish what is needed; (give an oracle, "graze" (touch slightly), light upon, etc.), i.e. (by implication) to employ or (by extension) to act towards one in a given manner
χράομαι.der: middle voice of a primary verb (perhaps rather from G5495 (χείρ), to handle);
χράομαι.as:
χράομαι, χρῶμαι
(< χρή), [in LXX for עשׂה, etc. ;]
to use, make use of: c. dat. (cf. M, Pr., 64, 158), Ac 27:17, I Co 9:12, 15, I Ti 1:85:23; μᾶλλον χρῆσαι (i.e. the opportunity; v. M, Pr., 247), I Co 7:21; as some­times in late writers (cf. M, Pr., 64; Lft., Notes, 233), c. acc., I Co 7:31; of feelings, etc., to exercise, shew: II Co 1:173:12; c. adv., ἀποτόμως, to deal sharply, II Co 13:10; c. dat. pers. (cl.), to treat, deal with, Ac 27:3.†

χῶρος.long: the north-west wind, and the quarter of the sky from which it comes.

χειμάζομαι.sd: to storm, i.e. (passively) to labor under a gale
χειμάζομαι.as:
χειμάζω
(< χεῖμα, winter cold) [in LXX: Pr 26:10 (†) * ;]
1.to expose to winter cold, go into winter quarters.
2.to drive with storm; pass., to be driven with storm, tempest-tossed: Ac 27:18.†

χάρισμα.long: a gift of grace, an undeserved favor.
χάρισμα.sd: a (divine) gratuity, i.e. deliverance (from danger or passion); (specially), a (spiritual) endowment, i.e. (subjectively) religious qualification, or (objectively) miraculous faculty
χάρισμα.as:
† χάρισμα, -τος, τό
(< χαρίζομαι) [in LXX: Si 7:33א(AB, χάρις) 38:30 Bl(אAB2R, χρῖσμα) * ;]
a gift of grace, a free gift, esp. of extra­ordinary operations of the Spirit in the Apostolic Church, but including all spiritual graces and endowments (Lft., Notes, 148 f.): Ro 1:115:15, 166:2311:2912:6, I Co 1:77:712:4, 9, 28, 30, 31, II Co 1:11, I Ti 4:14, II Ti 1:6, I Pe 4:10.†

χρῆσις.sd: employment, i.e. (specially), sexual intercourse (as an occupation of the body)
χρῆσις.as:
χρῆσις, -εως, ἡ
(< χράομαι), [in LXX: I Ki 1:28 (שׁאל), Si 18:8, al. ;]
use: in a sexual sense, Ro 1:26; c. gen. obj., θηλείας, ib. 27 (for exx., v. Thayer, s.v.).†

χρηστότης.sd: usefulness, i.e. morally, excellence (in character or demeanor)
χρηστότης.as:
χρηστότης, -ητος, ἡ
(< χρηστός), [in LXX for מוֺב and cogn. forms ;]
1.goodness, excellence, uprightness: Ro 3:12(LXX).
2.goodness of heart, kindness: Ro 2:4, II Co 6:6, Ga 5:22, Col 3:12, Tit 3:4; seq. ἐπί, c. acc. pers., Eph 2:7; id., opp. to ἀποτομία, Ro 11:22.
SYN.: v.s. ἀγαθωσύνη.

χρηματισμός.as:
χρηματισμός, -οῦ), ὁ
(< χρηματίζω, q.v.), [in LXX: Pr 24:60 (31:1) (מַשָּׂא), II Mac 2:411:17 * ;]
a divine response, an oracle: Ro 11:4 (Xen., Plat., al.).†

χρηστολογία.long: a kind address; in a bad sense: plausible speaking.
χρηστολογία.der: from a compound of G5543 (χρηστός) and G3004 (λέγω);
χρηστολογία.as:
*† χρηστολογία, -ας, ἡ
(χρηστός, λέγω),
fair speaking: in bad sense, Ro 16:18 (in good sense also, eccl.).†

Χλόη.long: Chloe, probably with business connections either in Corinth or in Ephesus or in both.
Χλόη.der: feminine of apparently a primary word;

χρηστεύομαι.long: I am kind (full of service to others), gentle.
χρηστεύομαι.sd: to show oneself useful, i.e. act benevolently

χοϊκός.sd: dusty or dirty (soil-like), i.e. (by implication) terrene
χοϊκός.as:
χοϊκός, -ή, -όν,
(< χοῦς)
earthy, made of dust: I Co 15:47-49 (v. Field, Notes, 179 f.).†

χορηγέω.sd: to be a dance-leader, i.e. (generally) to furnish
χορηγέω.der: from a compound of G5525 (χορός) and G71 (ἄγω);
χορηγέω.as:
χορηγέω, -ῶ
(< χορός, ἡγέομαι) [in LXX for כּוּל pilp. ;]
1.to lead aχορός (v. LS, s.v.).
2.to defray the cost of aχορός.
3. In late writers, metaph., c. acc. (v. M, Pr., 65), to supply, furnish abundantly: II Co 9:10, I Pe 4:11 (Polyb., al.).†

χειρόγραφον.sd: something hand-written ("chirograph"), i.e. a manuscript (specially, a legal document or bond (figuratively))
χειρόγραφον.der: neuter of a compound of G5495 (χείρ) and G1125 (γράφω);
χειρόγραφον.as:
**† χειρόγραφος, -ον
(< χείρ, γράφω), [in LXX: To 5:39:2, 5 * ;]
written with the hand. As subst., τὸ χ., a handwriting (Inscr., Polyb., al.): metaph., Col 2:14.†

χρήσιμον.as:
χρήσιμος, -η, -ον
(< χράομαι), [in LXX: Ge 37:26בֶּצַע etc. ;]
useful: II Ti 2:14.†

χρύσεος.long: golden, made of gold, adorned with gold.
χρύσεος.as:
χρύσεος, -εα, -εον (-οῦς, -ῆ, -οῦν; on acc sing. fem., -ᾶν, Re 1:13 and gen. pl. uncontr., -εων, Re 2:1, LTr., v. M, Pr., 48 and cf. Thackeray, Gr., x, 172 f.)
(< χρυσός), [in LXX chiefly for זָהָב ;]
golden, i.e. made or overlaid with gold: II Ti 2:20, He 9:4, Re 1:12, 13, 202:14:45:88:39:13, 2014:1415:6, 717:421:15.†

χαλκεύς.g: a worker in brass or copper
χαλκεύς.long: a worker in brass or copper; a smith.
χαλκεύς.as:
χαλκεύς, -έως, ὁ
(< χαλκός), [in LXX for חָרָשׁ, etc. ;]
a worker in metal, esp. a copper-smith: II Ti 4:14.†

χαρακτήρ.long: an impression, representation, exact reproduction; a graving-tool.
χαρακτήρ.sd: a graver (the tool or the person), i.e. (by implication) engraving (("character"), the figure stamped, i.e. an exact copy or (figuratively) representation)
χαρακτήρ.as:
χαρακτήρ, -ῆρος, ὁ
(< χαράσσω, to engrave), [in LXX: Le 13:28 (צָרֶבֶת), II Mac 4:10, IV Mac 15:4א R * ;]
1.a tool for graving.
2.a stamp or impress: as on a coin or seal; metaph., χ. τ. ὑποστάσεως, He 1:3.†

χρυσοῦς.long: golden, made of gold, adorned with gold.

Χεροῦβ.as:
† Χερουβείν (Rec. -βίμ), τά (Heb. כְּרוּבׅים),
Cherubim: He 9:6 (cf. Ex 25:17 (18), al.; v. DB, i, 377 ff.).†

χαλιναγωγέω.sd: to be a bit-leader, i.e. to curb (figuratively)
χαλιναγωγέω.der: from a compound of G5469 (χαλινός) and the reduplicated form of G71 (ἄγω);
χαλιναγωγέω.as:
*† χαλιναγωγέω, -ῶ
(< χαλινός, ἄγω),
to lead with a bridle; metaph., to bridle, restrain: c. acc., γλῶσσαν, Ja 1:26; σῶμα, 3:2.†

χρυσοδακτύλιος.sd: gold-ringed, i.e. wearing a golden finger-ring or similar jewelry

χαλινός.sd: a curb or head-stall (as curbing the spirit)
χαλινός.as:
χαλινός, -οῦ, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for מֶתֶג ;]
a bridle: Ja 3:3, Re 14:20.†

χρή.der: third person singular of the same as G5530 (χράομαι) or G5531 (χράω) used impersonally;
χρή.as:
* χρή impers.
(< χράω, v. LS, s.v.),
it is necessary: Ja 3:10 (cf. δεῖ.).†

χίλιοι.as:
χίλιοι, -αι, -α
a thousand: II Pe 3:8(LXX), Re 11:312:614:2020:2-7.†

χρῖσμα.sd: an unguent or smearing, i.e. (figuratively) the special endowment ("chrism") of the Holy Spirit
χρῖσμα.as:
χρίσμα (T, χρῖσμα, as in cl.; v. Tdf., Pr., 102; Bl., § 4, 2), -τος, το
(< χρίω),
later form of χρῖμα (Æsch., al.),
[in LXX for מִשְׁחָה and cogn. forms (Ex 29:7, al.) ;]
an anointing, unction (the result of the action χρίειν; ICC, in l.; but cf. Westc., in l, for the view that the oil, not the act, is meant): I Jo 2:20, 27.†

χάρτης.sd: a sheet ("chart") of writing-material (as to be scribbled over)
χάρτης.as:
χάρτης, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX: Is 8:1 A, Je 43 (36):2, 6, 23 (מְגִלָּה) * ;]
a sheet of paper, made of papyrus strips (v. Kennedy, Sources, 42; Milligan, NTD, 10-12; DB, iv, 945 f.): II Jo 12 (Plat., Inscr.).†

χαλκολίβανον.g: orichalcum, or frankincense of a yellow color
χαλκολίβανον.long: orichalcum, a fine metal, or frankincense of a yellow color.
χαλκολίβανον.sd: burnished copper, an alloy of copper (or gold) and silver having a brilliant lustre
χαλκολίβανον.der: neuter of a compound of G5475 (χαλκός) and G3030 (λίβανος) (in the implied mean of whiteness or brilliancy);
χαλκολίβανον.as:
*† χαλκο-λίβανον, -ου, τό
chalcolibanus, probably "a mixed metal of great brilliance" (Swete): Re 1:152:18 (RV, burnished brass).†

χλιαρός.as:
* χλιαρός, -ά, -όν
(< χλίω, to become warm),
warm, tepid; metaph., of persons, luke-warm: Re 3:16.†

χοῖνιξ.long: a Greek dry measure, equivalent to 1.92 pints.
χοῖνιξ.sd: a chœnix or certain dry measure
χοῖνιξ.as:
χοῖνιξ, -ικος, ἡ
[in LXX: Ez 45:10, 11 (בַּת) * ;]
a chænix, a dry measure of rather less than a quart: Re 6:6 (EV, measure).†

χάλαζα.as:
χάλαζα, -ης, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for בָּרָד ;]
hail: Re 8:711:1916:21.†

χαλκοῦς.as:
χάλκεος, -έα, -εον (-οῦς, -ῆ, -οῦν)
(< χαλκός), [in LXX chiefly for נְחֹשֶׁת ;]
brazen (i.e. of copper): Re 9:20.†

χρυσόω.sd: to gild, i.e. bespangle with golden ornaments
χρυσόω.as:
χρυσόω, -ῶ
(< χρυσός) [in LXX chiefly for צָפָה pi. ;]
to gild, cover with gold: pass., c. dat., χρυσίῳ (pleonast., cf. Ex 26:37), Re 17:418:16.†

χαλκηδών.long: chalcedony, a small stone of various colors.
χαλκηδών.as:
*† χαλκηδών, -όνος, ὁ
chalcedony, "supposed to denote a green silicate of copper found in the mines near Chalcedon " (Swete): Re 21:19.†

χρυσόλιθος.long: a topaz, a gem with a bright yellow color.
χρυσόλιθος.as:
χρυσό-λιθος, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX: Ex 28:2036:20 (39:13), Ez 28:13 (תַּרְשִׁישׁ) * ;]
a chrysolite (on its identification, v. Swete, Ap., 288 f.; DB, iv, 620): Re 21:20.†

χρυσόπρασος.long: a chrysoprase, gem of a golden-greenish color.
χρυσόπρασος.as:
*† χρυσό-πρασος, -ου, ὁ
a chrysoprase (v. Swete, Ap., 289): Re 21:20.†
